rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṣarīm means the orchard had become black like night.
rows.anchor: كالليل المسود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers called one another at dawn and went quietly so nobody would hear their plan to harvest.
rows.anchor: فانطلقوا لا يرفعون أصواتهم فيما بينهم لئلا يسمعهم أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On ḥard can mean that they thought themselves able to carry out the plan, or that they were angry with the poor.
rows.anchor: على حرد } أي : قادرين عند أنفسهم ، ويقال : على غضب منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing the orchard razed, they first denied it was theirs, then recognized it and realized they had been deprived of its good.
rows.anchor: قالوا : ليست هذه جنتنا ! ! ثم قالوا : بل هذه جنتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The middle brother was the most upright and best-spoken; he rebuked them for failing to say God willing.
rows.anchor: قال أوسطهم : أي أعدلهم طريقة وأحسنهم قولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers blamed one another, confessed their wrong, hoped God would replace the orchard with a better one, and turned to Him in hope.
rows.anchor: ثم أقبل بعضهم على بعض يتلاومون ، ويقولون . { عسى ربنا أن يبدلنا خيرا منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The orchard owners' fate is a warning of punishment for the people of Mecca and of the still greater punishment of the next life.
rows.anchor: لأهل مكة { ولعذاب الأخرة أكبر } وهكذا تكون حال من له بداية حسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A seeker may begin well and receive successive divine aid, avoiding sins as spiritual states appear inwardly; a presumptuous claim or breach of service etiquette can close those states and make actions feel heavy.
rows.anchor: حال من له بداية حسنة ويجد التوفيق على التوالي ، ويجتنب المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neglecting worship and obligations can reverse closeness into distance and estrangement, turning spiritual purity into hardness.
rows.anchor: إهمال - انقلب حاله ، ورد من الوصال إلى البعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance and regret after such a fall seldom restore the former state, though God may graciously accept the seeker in view of an earlier good beginning.
rows.anchor: فقد فات الأمر من يده ، وقلما يصل إلى حاله . ولا يبعد أن ينظر إليه الحق بأفضاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The God-fearing who avoid shirk and disbelief, then sins and transgression, receive reward from God.
rows.anchor: الذين يتقون الشرك والكفر ، ثم المعاصي والفسق ، لهم عند الله الثواب والأجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questions deny that Muslims and criminals can be treated alike: the objectors have neither evidence nor a revealed book or covenant authorizing their judgment.
rows.anchor: كيف تحكمون ؟ هل لديكم حجة ؟ { أم لكم كتاب فيه تدرسون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Uncovering the shin can signify the severity of Judgment Day; another exegetical view takes it as the shin of the Throne.
rows.anchor: عن ساق } : أي عن شدة يوم القيامة . ويقال في التفسير عن ساق العرش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers will prostrate when summoned, while unbelievers' backs stiffen and cannot bend; another view pictures a dying sick person unable to rise for the call to prayer.
rows.anchor: فأما المؤمنون فيسجدون ، وأما الكفار فتشد أصلابهم فلا تنحني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning may confront people at the end of worldly life or at the beginning of the next; recalling their earlier call to prostrate intensifies regret and makes the proof decisive.
rows.anchor: يذكرهم بذلك ليزدادوا حسرة ، ولتكون الحجة عليهم أبلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brings deniers gradually toward punishment without their noticing, concealing the direction until He takes them suddenly.
rows.anchor: وبالاستدراج : أن يريد الشيء ويطوي عن صاحبه وجه القصد فيه ، ويدرجه إليه شيئا بعد شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account calls istidrāj the granting of blessings together with forgetfulness of gratitude.
rows.anchor: التمكين من النعم مقرونا بنسيان الشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says that each increase in their sin is met by an increase in blessing.
rows.anchor: كلما ازدادوا معصية زادهم نعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account defines istidrāj as withholding punishment at the moment of a slip and delaying it until afterward.
rows.anchor: ويقال : ألا يعاقبه في حال الزلة ، وإنما يؤخر العقوبة إلى ما بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other definitions are becoming occupied with blessings while forgetting their giver, being lured by a long reprieve, and appearing enviable outwardly while inwardly troubled.
rows.anchor: هو الاشتغال بالنعمة مع نسيان المنعم . ويقال : الاغرار بطول الإمهال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives the deniers time, then seizes them with painful severity.
rows.anchor: أمهلهم . . . ثم إذا أخذتهم فأخذي أليم شديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet asks no fee, so the audience bears no cost for following him; the lack of expense makes their refusal inexplicable.
rows.anchor: ليس عليهم كلفة مقابل ما تدعوهم إليه ، وليست عليهم غرامة إن هم اتبعوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers possess no private knowledge of the unseen that could justify refusing the message.
rows.anchor: أم عندهم شيء من الغيب انفردوا به وأوجب لهم ألا يستجيبوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion of the whale is Jonah, whose heart was full of anger toward his people; Muhammad must not rush their punishment as Jonah did but patiently accept God's decree.
rows.anchor: صاحب الحوت : هو يونس عليه السلام : { نادى وهو مكظوم } : مملوء بالغيظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without God's merciful favor Jonah would have been cast into the open ground blameworthy; God instead chose him, made him righteous, and sent him to a hundred thousand or more.
rows.anchor: لولا أن الله رحمه بفضله لطرح بالفضاء وهو مذموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabs were said to fast three days before an evil-eye attack; they tried it on Muhammad by praising his eloquence, but God protected him.
rows.anchor: جاعوا ثلاثة أيام ، ثم جاؤوا ونظروا إلى ذلك الشيء قائلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laẓā is a name for Hell; nazzāʿa li-l-shawā means it tears away the extremities and strips skin from face and bone.
rows.anchor: تكشط الجلد عن الوجه وعن العظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell calls the unbeliever and hypocrite who turned away, summoning them toward itself.
rows.anchor: تقول جهنم للكافر والمنافق : يا فلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As an inward sign, worldly life is a hell that hooks the heart with greed, drags it into accumulation, and makes people prefer wealth even to family; few escape its deception.
rows.anchor: والإشارة فيه : أن جهنم الدنيا تعلق بقلب المرء فتدعوه بكلاب الحرص إلى نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following verses explain halūʿ as intense acquisitiveness joined to agitation: distress brings despair, while prosperity brings withholding.
rows.anchor: والهلع شدة الحرص مع الجزع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other glosses describe the person as tossed among desires, dissatisfied by even a little, praying in hardship but forgetting God in ease.
rows.anchor: ويقال هلوعا : متقلبا في غمرات الشهوات . ويقال : يرضيه القليل ويسخطه اليسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception for those constant in prayer describes people who continually inhabit the stations of neediness before God.
rows.anchor: يلازمون أبدا مواطن الافتقار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The known share in wealth belongs to both the asking poor and the self-restrained poor.
rows.anchor: وهم المتكفف والمتعفف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some give all their property to anyone who comes; others both give and retain; the most complete regard their hand as entrusted property and await guidance to give or withhold as the moment requires.
rows.anchor: يرى يده يد الأمانه فلا يتكلف باختياره ، وإنما ينتظر ما يشار عليه به من الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers prepare for death before it arrives, standing ready to depart like travelers already poised to leave.
rows.anchor: الاستعداد للموت قبل نزوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They keep sexual relations within marriage or lawful ownership to preserve chastity and seek a child who will remember God; they should not impose their own desires on a spouse.
rows.anchor: صحبتهم مع أزواجهم للتعفف وصون النفس ، ثم لابتغاء أن يكون له ولد من صلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They honor trusts held for people and protect bodily faculties from sin; knowledge, divine secrets, obligations, unity, primordial testimony, and divinely placed love are also trusts.
rows.anchor: المعرفة التي في قلوبهم أمانة عندهم من الحق ، والأسرار التي بينهم وبين الله أمانات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihṭāʿ is fixing one's gaze on something without lifting it; ʿizīn means groups gathered separately.
rows.anchor: والإهطاع أن يقبل ببصره إلى الشيء فلا يرفعه عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers are wrong to assume they will receive what they desire: they are unbelievers now and will be treated tomorrow according to what they deserve.
rows.anchor: فإنهم - اليوم - كفار ، وغدا يعاملون بما يستوجبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle lā in the oath is redundant, so the meaning is an oath by the Lord of the Easts and Wests; God is able to replace them.
rows.anchor: لا - هنا صلة ، والمعنى أقسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to leave the deniers to their talk and play is a pointed threat and rebuke.
rows.anchor: غاية التهديد والتوبيخ لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hurried emergence from graves resembles their present rush to idols and sacrificial altars to worship them.
rows.anchor: شبه إسراعهم حين قاموا من القبور بإسراعهم إلى النصب - اليوم - كي يقوموا بعبادتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation is heavy to hear for one who rejects it; another reading says its burden is borne only by someone aided by heavenly strength and nurtured in divine nearness.
rows.anchor: ثقيلا } سماعه على من جحده . ويقال : ( ثقيلا بعبئه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night-formed hours are each newly arising; night prayer is better aligned with tongue and heart and brings greater energy.
rows.anchor: ساعات الليل ، فكل ساعة تحدث فهي ناشئة ، وهي أشد وطئا أي : موطأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night prayer may also be harder and weightier than prayer during the day.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل : هي أشد وأغلظ على الإنسان من القيام بالنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says night prayer accords more closely with the heart because it is farther from ostentation and brings deeper inward presence and stillness.
rows.anchor: لأنها أبعد من الرياء ، ويكون فيها حضور القلب وسكون السر أبلغ وأتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daytime offers many occupations and journeys, while night leaves the Prophet freer for worship.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى : مذاهبك في النهار فيما يشغلك كثيرة - والليل أخلى لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabattul means complete devotion and severance toward God.
rows.anchor: انقطع إليه انقطاعا تاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wakīl is entrusted with affairs, so the servant should entrust every matter to God and rely on Him.
rows.anchor: أي : توكل عليه وكل أمورك إليه ، وثق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike a human agent who takes one's money and charges a fee, God preserves one's wealth and rewards the one who entrusts affairs to Him.
rows.anchor: إذا اتخذت من المخلوقين وكيلا اختزلوا مالك وطالبوك بالأجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A human agent spends the client's own money, whereas God provides and spends from His own provision.
rows.anchor: وكيلك ينفق عليك من مالك ، وأنا أرزقك وأنفق عليك من مالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People may avoid speaking much to a subordinate agent, but God as Lord desires intimate conversation with His servant.
rows.anchor: وأنا ربك سيدك وأحب أن تكلمني وأكلمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beautiful estrangement means outwardly keeping company while inwardly remaining apart, or leaving people for God's sake rather than one's own interest.
rows.anchor: تعاشرهم بظاهرك وتباينهم بسرك وقلبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another meaning is not speaking to them but speaking to God on their behalf through prayer; the verse was later abrogated by the fighting verse.
rows.anchor: ألا تكلمهم ، وتكلمني لأجلهم بالدعاء لهم . وهذه الآية منسوخة بآية القتال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of affluence are told to wait briefly because God will handle their affair.
rows.anchor: أي : أولي التنعم وأنظرهم قليلا ، ولا تهتم بشأنهم ، فإني أكفيك أمرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment includes choking food, painful torment, an earth and mountains shaken, and mountains reduced to a heap of loose sand.
rows.anchor: وطعاما ذا غصة وعذابا أليما } . ثم ذكر وصف القيامة فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad was sent as a witness just as Moses was sent to Pharaoh; Pharaoh disobeyed and received a severe, weighty punishment.
rows.anchor: أرسلنا إليكم محمدا شاهدا عليكم { كما أرسلنا إلى فرعون رسولا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Judgment Day's horror turning children gray and the sky splitting from its terror are expressions of its overwhelming severity; another reading says it splits by God's command.
rows.anchor: من هوله يصير الولدان شيبا - وهذا على ضرب المثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God has promised will certainly be fulfilled.
rows.anchor: فما وعد الله سيصدقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah or its verses are a reminder; whoever takes heed succeeds.
rows.anchor: يعني هذه السورة ، أو هذه الآيات موعظة ؛ فمن اتعظ بها سعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eased recitation may be five verses or more; another view sets the minimum at ten or more.
rows.anchor: ويقال : من عشر آيات إلى ما يزيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because illness and travel affect some believers, the night vigil was lifted from those with such excuses.
rows.anchor: يسافرون ، ويعلم أصحاب الأعذار ، فنسخ عنهم قيام الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to establish prayer refers to the obligatory prayer; good lending to God was explained earlier, and good deeds sent ahead return as reward better than worldly possessions.
rows.anchor: ما تقدموا من طاعة تجدوها عند الله ثوابا هو خير لكم من كل متاع الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the man capable of freely conducting affairs and managing his activities.
rows.anchor: تسهيل التصرف ، أي : مكنته من التصرف في الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He expects God to increase his blessings further.
rows.anchor: يطمع أن أزيده في النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He stubbornly rejects God's signs and will be made to undergo a steep, burdensome punishment.
rows.anchor: سأحمله على مشقة من العذاب

rows.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
rows.claim: Al-Walīd thought over the Prophet's message and concluded that it was neither poetry, madness, nor lying, but called it transmitted magic and human speech.
rows.anchor: يعني به : الوليد بن المغيرة الذي قال في النبي : إنه ليس بشاعر ولا بمجنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saqar leaves neither flesh nor bone; its fire burns and alters the skin of the face.
rows.anchor: من لاحته الشمس ولوحته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists objected that their large number could not be overcome by only nineteen keepers; God explains that the keepers are angels and their number tests deniers while confirming and strengthening believers and scriptural communities.
rows.anchor: قال المشركون : نحن جمع كثير . . . فما يفعل بنا تسعة عشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God comprehends the full number of His forces; created knowledge reaches some measures but not others.
rows.anchor: تقاصرت علوم الخلق فلم تتعلق إلا بمقدار دون مقدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lā is a particle of rebuke and attention; God swears by the moon, the night as it departs, and the dawn as it brightens.
rows.anchor: كلا - حرف ردع وتنبيه ؛ أي : ؛ ارتدعوا عما أنتم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading without the alif, dabbara, means that the night has passed.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( ودبر ) أي : مضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asfara means that the morning has become clear and bright.
rows.anchor: والصبح إذا أسفر } أي : تجلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase calls Hell one of the greatest calamities.
rows.anchor: أي : النار لإحدى الدواهي الكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In an inward reading, moons of knowledge wax as proofs grow; when knowledge reaches fullness, the sun of gnosis rises and makes the moons of learning seem to wane like lamps in daylight.
rows.anchor: إذا صارت إلى حد التمام في العلم وبلغت الغاية تبدوا إعلام المعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The departing night signifies inner darkness lifting, and the dawn signifies the lights of realities appearing in the innermost heart.
rows.anchor: أي إذا انكشفت ظلم البواطن ، { والصبح إذا أسفر } وتجلت أنوار الحقائق في السرائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning also fears that darkness may return to hearts after reality has been disclosed.
rows.anchor: من باب التخويف من عودة الظلم إلى القلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning to humankind cautions against worldly distractions that interrupt access to reality and against settling into pride over acts of obedience, which have no independent weight.
rows.anchor: تحذير من الشواغل التي هي قواطع عن الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The choice to advance or fall behind in obedience is phrased as a threat.
rows.anchor: وهذا على جهة التهديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each soul is held by what it has earned, except the people of the right.
rows.anchor: إنهم غير مرتهنين بأعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the right may be those promised, without qualification, that they are in Paradise; another view identifies them as believers' children.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء في الجنة ولا أبالي ) ! وقيل : أطفال المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People in Paradise ask criminals what brought them to Saqar; they cite neglecting prayer and feeding the poor, joining false talk, and denying Judgment Day, showing that unbelievers face detailed religious obligations.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن الكفار مخاطبون بتفصيل الشرائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No intercessor's intercession will reach the criminals.
rows.anchor: لا تنالهم شفاعة من يشفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They turn away from the reminder, the Quran, like startled wild donkeys fleeing a lion.
rows.anchor: كأنهم حمر نافرة فرت من أسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each denier wants a personally delivered open scripture, but this wish is denied because they do not fear the next life.
rows.anchor: كلا لا يعطون ما يتمنون لأنهم لا يخافون الأخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is a reminder, but human willing depends on God's will; God is worthy of piety and may forgive whoever fears Him.
rows.anchor: إلا أن يشاء الله - لا أن تشاؤوا . { هو أهل التقوى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There will be no refuge or escape from God's judgment; all will come to rest before their Lord.
rows.anchor: ولا مهرب من قضاء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day a person is informed of deeds sent ahead or left behind, including sins God recorded even if the person forgot them.
rows.anchor: أي : يعرف ما أسلفه من ذنوب أحصاها الله - وإن كان العبد نسيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person is a witness against himself because his own limbs testify to his actions.
rows.anchor: فأعضاؤه تشهد عليه بما عمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes the person as his own proof concerning denial of resurrection; another says he knows he was an unbeliever, so excuses cannot help.
rows.anchor: هو بصيرة وحجة على نفسه في إنكار البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was told not to hurry his tongue to catch the revelation: God would collect it in his heart, enable its recitation, and explain its rulings.
rows.anchor: وكذلك علينا تيسير قرءاته على لسانك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad had hurried to receive the Quran for fear of forgetting, so God forbade this and guaranteed ease and preservation.
rows.anchor: وكان رسول الله يستعجل في التلقف مخافة النسيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Love of the immediate life drives their denial: they want to remain in this world and leave work for the Hereafter, or disbelieve in it.
rows.anchor: إنما يحملهم على التكذيب للقيامة والنشر أنهم يحبون العاجلة في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bright faces are beautiful because they see God; the phrase's construction indicates actual vision, which God creates in their faces beyond ordinary conditions.
rows.anchor: والنظر المقرون ب ( إلى ) مضافا إلى الوجه لا يكون إلا الرؤية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eye belongs to the face, so attributing vision to the face is sound; this is like saying a river runs when its water is what flows.
rows.anchor: الوجه لا ينظر ولكن العين في الوجه هي التي تنظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their brightness indicates composure without confusion; for people of spiritual realization, continued abiding in encounter surpasses the initial vision.
rows.anchor: فالنضرة من أمارات البسط لأن البقاء في حال اللقاء أتم من اللقاء

rows.speaker: أهل التحقيق
rows.claim: The people of verification say vision entails the seer's continued existence, while annihilation of the servant in God's being is more complete; those who speak of being rank presence above vision.
rows.anchor: والرؤية عند أهل التحقيق تقتضي بقاء الرائي ، وعندهم استهلاك العبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Somber faces are grim, and fāqirah is a calamity: their perpetual residence in Hell; they may expect a gaze to be created in their faces, or have an expectation formed in their hearts that shows on their faces.
rows.anchor: فاقرة } أي : داهية وهي بقاؤهم في النار على التأييد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As the soul reaches the collarbones, bystanders ask who can perform healing or give medicine; alternatively angels ask whether mercy or punishment angels will take the soul.
rows.anchor: هل أحد يرقيه ؟ هل طبيب يداويه ؟ هل دواء يشفيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dying person knows death has come; the two legs joined are the deceased's legs, and the end of worldly hardship meets the beginning of the next life's hardship.
rows.anchor: فتقترن شدة آخر الدنيا بشدة أول الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels carry the soul to God, either to the درجات of ʿIlliyyīn or the درجات of Sijjīn; another image has God clothing, cleansing, and praying over the soul in mercy.
rows.anchor: إما إلى عليين - ثم لها تفاوت درجات ، وإما إلى سجين - ولها تفاوت دركات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbeliever neither affirmed God nor prayed, but denied and turned away; this indicates that unbelievers are bound by detailed religious obligations.
rows.anchor: وتدل الآية على أن الكفار مخاطبون بتفصيل الشرائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He returned to his family strutting with arrogance.
rows.anchor: أي : يتبختر ويختال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated warning is an intensified curse; alternatively, woe awaits the unbeliever when living, dying, resurrected, and entering Hell.
rows.anchor: ويقال : معناه الويل لك يوم تحيا . والويل لك يوم تموت ، والويل لك يوم تبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person is not left neglected and without moral responsibility.
rows.anchor: مهملا لا يكلف ! ؟ . ليس كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human develops from semen to a clot and is formed in the womb; God makes male, female, or both, proving His power to raise the dead.
rows.anchor: وجعل منه الزوجين : إن شاء خلق الذكر ، وإن شاء خلق الأنثى ، وإن شاء كليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala describes God as eternally one in majesty and sovereignty, with unchanging, sacred, and everlasting attributes.
rows.anchor: أحدي الوصف ، صمدي الذات ، مقدس النعت ، واحد الجلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse can mean a time passed when humanity had no significance or worth.
rows.anchor: قد أتى على الإنسان حين من الدهر لم يكن شيئا له خطر ومقدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Adam's body lay between Mecca and Ṭāʾif forty years, then remained clay and molded clay for forty years each, completing his creation in 120 years.
rows.anchor: كان آدم عليه السلام أربعين سنة مطروحا جسده بين مكة والطائف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An inward reading asks whether any moment passed without God remembering, preserving, and newly protecting the person.
rows.anchor: هل غفلت ساعة عن حفظك ؟ هل ألقيت - لحظة - حبلك على غاربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mixed drop combines fluid from man and woman; the human passes through stages of drop, clot, bone, and flesh.
rows.anchor: { أمشاج } : أخلاط من بين الرجل والمرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabtali means that God tests and examines the human being.
rows.anchor: { نبتليه } : نمتحنه ونختبره . وقد مضى معناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes the human able to hear and see.
rows.anchor: فجعلناه سميعا بصيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes the paths of good and evil known; the person is either grateful or ungrateful.
rows.anchor: أي : عرفناه الطريق ؛ أي طريق الخير والشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation reads the alternatives as bliss or misery, or as gratitude from God's friends through enabling grace versus disbelief from His enemies through abandonment.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إما للشقاوة ، وإما للسعادة ، إما شاكرا من أوليائنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has prepared chains for dragging unbelievers, collars to humiliate them, and blazing fire.
rows.anchor: أي : هيأنا لهم سلاسل يسحبون فيها ، { وأغلالا } لأعناقهم يهانون بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous may be those who harbor no evil and harm no creature, or those whose aspirations rise beyond trivial things and whose wisdom leads them away from settling in worldly life.
rows.anchor: قيل : البر : الذي لا يضمر الشر ، ولا يؤذي الذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The camphor cup may smell like camphor or be mixed with it; in both worldly and next-worldly life, spiritual drink differs according to each person's state and company.
rows.anchor: { يشربون من كأس } رائحتها كرائحة الكافور ، أو ممزوجة بالكافور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spiritual drink may be intimacy now and a cup in the Hereafter, or divine kindness now and a cup handed around later.
rows.anchor: ويقال : اليوم شراب وغدا شراب . . . اليوم شراب الإيناس وغدا شراب الكاس ، اليوم شراب من اللطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The drink of divine love gives intimacy and courage, removes fear, and makes the lover willing to sacrifice life.
rows.anchor: من سقاه اليوم شراب محبته آنسه وشجعه ؛ فلا يستوحش في وقته من شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Love's cup makes the drinker give both worlds freely to everyone without distinction or inward attachment to worldly dangers.
rows.anchor: يجود على كل أحد بالكونين من غير تمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some drinkers become utterly humble toward all, while others may sometimes feel exalted above both abodes.
rows.anchor: فيكون لأصغر الخدم تراب القدم ، لا يتحرك فيه للتكبر عرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ecstatic joy may strip away reserve and shame, exposing the drinker's inward states; a cited poem describes people casting off the veil of decorum.
rows.anchor: ومن مقتضى ذلك الشراب أيضا أن يملكه سرور ولا يتمالك معه من خلع العذار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The drink can also remove decorum, bringing expansive speech and complaints that sober people would have to extract from a fool with pincers.
rows.anchor: فيتكلم بمقتضى البسط ، أو بموجب لفظ الشكوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mystics explain Moses' request to see God as speech produced while intoxicated by hearing God's words.
rows.anchor: فقالوا : سكر من سماع كلامه ، فنطق بذلك لسانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who drink the wine of unity lose awareness of every other thing and dissolve into the valleys of majesty and the atmosphere of divine oneness, beyond intellect or perception.
rows.anchor: فلا عقل ولا تمييز ولا فهم ولا إدراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant first becomes wholly absorbed in unveiling, then immersed, and finally annihilated.
rows.anchor: فالعبد يكون في ابتداء الكشف مستوعبا ثم يصير مستغرقا ثم يصير مستهلكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reward is God's multiplication of recompense for a small amount of work, according to scholars.
rows.anchor: تكثير الثواب على القليل من العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another group says God's gratitude to the righteous is itself their reward; another says He honors them by praising their good works.
rows.anchor: وعند قوم شكرهم جزاؤهم على شكرهم . ويقال : شكره لهم ثناؤه عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent the Quran down over a period of years.
rows.anchor: في مدة سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience with God's decree means accepting and submitting to it; the Prophet must obey his Lord alone, not a sinner or unbeliever.
rows.anchor: وهذا أمر له بإفراد ربه بطاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remember God morning and evening, then perform voluntary night prostration and prolonged praise after the obligatory worship.
rows.anchor: الفرض في الأول ، ثم النفل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh love immediate life and ignore the weighty Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: أي كفار قريش : { يحبون العاجلة ويذرون وراءهم يوما ثقيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created and strengthened them and can destroy them and replace them; another interpretation says He took their covenant.
rows.anchor: أعدمناهم ، وخلقنا غيرهم بدلا عنهم . ويقال : أخذنا عنهم الميثاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is a reminder, and the path to God is obedience.
rows.anchor: أي : القرآن تذكرة . { فمن شاء اتخذ إلى ربه سبيلا } . بطاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human willing exists only under God's will; He admits whom He wills into mercy and prepares painful punishment for wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: وما تشاءون إلا أن يشاء الله إن الله كان عليما حكيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala chills the hearts of obedient people and kindles those of the disobedient; it delights aspirants and disturbs gnostics.
rows.anchor: وأوهجت من آخرين قلوبا ، من المطيعين أثلجتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Resurrection the sun loses its light, stars scatter, mountains move, pregnant camels are abandoned, seas ignite, souls are paired, the buried girl is questioned, records spread, heaven is stripped, and Hell and Paradise appear.
rows.anchor: ذهب ضوؤها . { وإذا النجوم انكدرت } . تناثرت وسقطت على الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wild animals are raised and gathered so the hornless may receive justice from the horned; this is an analogy because animals have no legal duty.
rows.anchor: فيقتص للجماء من القرناء - وهذا على جهة ضرب المثل ؛ إذ لا تكليف عليها

rows.speaker: أهل البدع
rows.claim: It is possible that animals receive compensating benefits for pain suffered in this life, but this is a possibility rather than an obligation.
rows.anchor: على العوض . . جوازا لا وجوبا على ما قاله أهل البدع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath by retreating, moving, hiding stars may instead refer to wild cattle.
rows.anchor: أي : أقسم ، والخنس والكنس هي النجوم إذا غربت . ويقال : البقر الوحشي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asʿasa means the night arrives and approaches; the morning's breathing is its emergence from the heart of night.
rows.anchor: { نفس } : خرج من جوف الليل . أقسم بهذه الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's answer is that the Quran is the speech of Gabriel, an honored, powerful messenger in a secure position near the Throne.
rows.anchor: وجواب القسم : { إنه لقول رسول كريم } . إن هذا القرآن لقول رسول كريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel's strength is illustrated by his lifting and overturning the settlement of Lot's people.
rows.anchor: بلغ من قوته أنه قلع قرية آل لوط وقلبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath also answers that Muhammad, their companion, is not mad.
rows.anchor: وهذا أيضا من جواب القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad saw Gabriel on the clear horizon on the Night Journey; another view says he saw his Lord there.
rows.anchor: رأى محمد جبريل عليه السلام بالأفق المبين ليلة المعراج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger is not suspected of withholding knowledge of the unseen.
rows.anchor: بمتهم . قوله جل ذكره : { فأين تذهبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question Where are you going? rebukes people for wandering in conjecture instead of returning to their Master and witnessing reality in good and bad times.
rows.anchor: إلى متى تتطوحون في أودية الظنون والحسبان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is a reminder for all worlds and a guide for anyone who wishes to be upright.
rows.anchor: ما هذا القرآن إلا ذكرى { لمن شاء منكم أن يستقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People can will only what God, Lord of the worlds, wills.
rows.anchor: وما تشآءون إلا أن يشآء الله رب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Sufi experience, the cosmic signs recur inwardly: aspirants' stars of knowledge dim when desire takes over, after which each knows what they have brought.
rows.anchor: نجوم علومهم قد تنكدر لاستيلاء الهوى على المريدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala describes God's incomparable majesty and beauty, purposeless actions, power without acquisition, and knowledge independent of necessity or inference; He neither began nor will end.
rows.anchor: وقدرته لا باجتلاب ولا احتيال ، وعلمه لا بضرورة ولا استدلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heaven splits and obeys its Lord; earth is flattened, expels its dead and treasures, and also obeys; the answer is that the human meets what his deeds merit.
rows.anchor: قابلت أمر ربها بالسمع والطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every accountable person labors toward God and will meet the recompense: good for good and evil for evil.
rows.anchor: إنك ساع بما لك سعيا ستلقى جزاءه ؛ بالخير خيرا وبالشر شرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer who receives the book in the right hand faces an easy reckoning without hardship.
rows.anchor: وهو المؤمن المحسن . { فسوف يحاسب حسابا يسيرا } . أي حسابا لا مشقة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An easy reckoning may mean hearing God's speech directly, whose address lightens the burden, or being asked about good deeds without being reproached for sins.
rows.anchor: { حسابا يسيرا } أي يسمعه كلامه - سبحانه - بلا واسطة ، فيخفف سماع خطابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer returns joyful because of salvation, rank, intimate conversation, accepted worship, and forgiven slips; he may intercede for those he loves, avoid disgrace, or meet and speak with God before entering Paradise.
rows.anchor: أي بالنجاة والدرجات ، وما وجد من المناجاة ، وقبول الطاعات ، وغفران الزلات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbeliever receives the record behind his back, cries for destruction, and enters Hell.
rows.anchor: وهو الكافر . { فسوف يدعوا ثبورا } . أي ويلا . { ويصلى سعيرا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He had been complacent and arrogant among his family and believed he would not return to God or be resurrected.
rows.anchor: من البطر والمدح . { إنه ظن أن لن يحور } . أنه لن يرجع إلينا ، ولن يبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shafaq is the redness that follows sunset.
rows.anchor: بالحمرة التي تعقب غروب الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night gathers and encloses what it covers.
rows.anchor: وما جمع وضم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In inward readings, the setting sun is the end of intimacy and onset of separation, contraction after expansion, or separation after union; nights may signify absence, intimate union, or ardent seeking.
rows.anchor: ويقال : الشفق حين غربت شمس وصالهم ، وأذيقوا الفراق في بعض أحوالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the moon becomes full, it signifies gnosis' sovereignty appearing in hearts without loss or diminution.
rows.anchor: إذا ظهر سلطان العرفان على القلوب فلا بخس ولا نقصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Passing through successive stages can mean the levels of heaven, hardship after hardship, human aging, seeking then arrival and connection, changes of poverty and health, or conditions in the next life.
rows.anchor: تارات الإنسان طفلا ثم شابا ثم كهلا ثم شيخا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers fail to believe or prostrate when Quran is recited despite the clear proofs; they deny what is true.
rows.anchor: فما الكفار أمتك لا يصدقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what their hearts contain, just as something placed in a vessel is contained by it.
rows.anchor: تنطوي عليه قلوبهم - من أوعيت المتاع في الظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers are promised painful punishment, while believers who do good receive an unending reward.
rows.anchor: فإنهم ليسوا منهم ، ولهم أجر غير مقطوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala unsettles the poor and disorients the enamored, but brings mercy to lovers; worshippers may satisfy it by reciting, while lovers must offer their lives.
rows.anchor: كلمة قهارة للقلوب ، ولكن لا لكل قلب ، كلمة لا سبيل لهها لكل عقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fajr is the first burst of morning light, described as both elongated and short; interpretations identify the dawn of Muharram, Dhu al-Hijjah, water emerging from rocks, or the saints' opening worship.
rows.anchor: الفجر انفجار الصبح وهو اثنان : مستطيل وقصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ten nights may be the first ten of Dhu al-Hijjah, Muharram ending in ʿĀshūrāʾ, Ramadan's last ten, or Moses' ten nights completing his appointed term.
rows.anchor: قيل : هي عشر ذي الحجة ، ويقال : عشر المحرم ؛ لأن آخرها عاشوراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An inward dawn is the gnostics' hearts rising beyond ordinary knowledge, when their gnosis shines and they no longer need proof's darkness.
rows.anchor: ويقال : هو ( فجر ) قلوب العارفين إذا ارتقوا عن حد العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The even and odd may be the Day of Sacrifice and the Day of ʿArafah, Adam paired with Eve, or even and odd-numbered prayers such as dawn and sunset prayer.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفاسير : الشفع يوم النحر ، والوتر يوم عرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes even and odd as numerical pairs and singles, or as creation's opposed attributes compared with God's unopposed attributes.
rows.anchor: ويقال : الشفع تضاد أوصاف الخلق : كالعلم والجهل ، والقدرة والعجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One inward reading pairs intention and will, leaving aspiration isolated because it cannot be satisfied by creatures or reach God through union or separation.
rows.anchor: لا تكتفي بالمخلوق ولا سبيل لها إلى الله - لتقدسه عن الوصل والفصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ascetic and worshipper are paired with a counterpart, whereas the seeker is solitary in every town.
rows.anchor: ويقال : الشفع الزاهد والعابد ، لأن لكل منهما شكلا وقرينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night that moves on simply passes away.
rows.anchor: ( يسري ) يمضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person of reason recognizes that the oath warns that God watches over and does not miss anything; the passage recalls earlier nations and the severity of their punishment.
rows.anchor: { إن ربك لبالمرصاد } . لا يفوته شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People wrongly read abundance as God's honor and restricted provision as humiliation; the true humiliation is being abandoned to disobedience.
rows.anchor: ليس الإذلال بالفقر إنما بالخذلان للعصيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They deserve blame for failing to honor orphans, urge feeding the poor, consuming inheritance greedily, and loving wealth excessively; lamm means forcefully and jamm abundantly.
rows.anchor: أي : أنتم تستحقون الإهانة على هذه الخصال المذمومة ؛ فلا تكرمون اليتيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At resurrection, God's coming may mean angels arrive by His command or that He performs an act called coming; Hell is dragged with seventy thousand reins, and remembrance then cannot help.
rows.anchor: ويقال : يفعل فعلا فيسميه مجيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The regret is a wish to have obeyed God and looked after one's own future life.
rows.anchor: أي : أطعت ربي ونظرت لنفسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the dāl vowelled with kasra, no one is punished as God punishes; with fatḥa, no one punishes this unbeliever as God does.
rows.anchor: إذا قرئت الذال بالكسر . أما إذا قرئت بالفتح { لا يعذب } فالمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tranquil soul may be the spirit settled toward the still soul, or a soul made tranquil by gnosis, remembrance of God, or glad tidings of Paradise.
rows.anchor: المطمئنة بالمعرفة : ويقال : المطمئنة بذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being pleased means content with God, and approved means accepted by God.
rows.anchor: راضية عن الله ، مرضية من قبل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul is invited to enter among God's righteous servants and then enter His Garden.
rows.anchor: أي : في عبادي الصالحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala announces eternal majesty and beauty, whose disclosure brings self-effacement or abiding states to those it reaches.
rows.anchor: جلال من كاشفه به فأوصافه فناء في فناء ، وجمال من لاطفه به فأحواله بقاء في بقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath is by Mecca, where the Prophet was made lawful for one hour, and by every parent and child; another view identifies the parent and child as Adam and his descendants.
rows.anchor: أي : أقسم بهذا البلد ، وهو مكة . { وأنت حل بهذا البلد } . وإنما أحلت له ساعة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath may also be because the Prophet was present in Mecca: the beloved makes the beloved place dear.
rows.anchor: ويقال : أقسم بهذا البلد لأنك حل به . . وبلد الحبيب حبيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings were created amid hardship and endure the trials of this world and the next.
rows.anchor: أي : في مشقة ؛ فهو يقاسي شدائد الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading traces bodily hardship from the upright fetus through inversion at birth, swaddling, and the difficult road ahead.
rows.anchor: فإذا أذن الله أن يخرج من بطن أمه تنكس رأسه عند خروجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The powerful man boasts of spending abundant wealth against Muhammad and assumes no one sees him, though God watches him.
rows.anchor: { لبدا } كثيرا ، في عداوة محمد . { أيحسب أن لم يره أحد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created eyes, tongue, and lips so the person can see and speak, and showed the two paths of good and evil.
rows.anchor: أي : ألم نخلقه سميعا بصيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about the formidable ascent magnifies its seriousness: cross it by freeing a slave or feeding a related orphan or dust-poor person during famine.
rows.anchor: أي : إعتاق مملوك ، والفك الإزالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person in dust is so poor as to seem stuck to the ground with hunger; the passage calls for feeding such people in famine and hardship.
rows.anchor: لا شيء له حتى كأنه قد التصق بالتراب من الجوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessed combine faith with mutual counsel to patience and compassion; they are the people of the right and blessing.
rows.anchor: أي : من الذين يرحم بعضهم بعضا . { أولئك أصحاب الميمنة } . أي : أصحاب اليمن والبركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who disbelieve in God's signs are ill-omened for themselves and face a sealed, enclosing fire.
rows.anchor: هم المشائيم على أنفسهم ، عليهم نار مطبقة ؛ يعني أبواب النيران ( عليهم مغلقة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, the ascent is the obstacle of the self and desire; one must escape enslavement to ego, worldly attachments, and self-directed choice for the spaciousness of contentment.
rows.anchor: والعقبة التي يجب على الإنسان اقتحامها : نفسه وهواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Freeing a neck also means freeing oneself from the bondage of desire and people, with a guide leading from greed and humiliation into safety.
rows.anchor: و { فك رقبة } هو إعتاق نفسه من رق الأغراض والأشخاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Self-liberation entails leaving one's own planning and choice for the broad contentment of surrender.
rows.anchor: بالتحرز من التدبير ، والخروج من ظلمات الاختيار إلى سعة الرضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seeker should feed someone in dust even while personally hungry.
rows.anchor: يطعم من كان في متربة ويكون هو في مسبغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The outcome depends on ending one's life among the faithful.
rows.anchor: أي تكون خاتمته على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala speaks of God's eternal existence and enduring sublimity; spirits are stunned by majesty, while souls thirst for the kindness of beauty.
rows.anchor: فالأرواح دهشى في كشف جلاله ، والنفوس عطشى إلى لطف جماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun's ḍuḥā is early after sunrise, the moon follows it in the first half of the month, day reveals the sun, and night covers its light.
rows.anchor: { والقمر إذا تلاها } . أي : تبعها ؛ وذلك في النصف الأول من الشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath may be by the heaven and its construction, or by its builder; by the earth and its spreading, or by its spreader; and by the soul and the one who shaped its parts and organs.
rows.anchor: أي : وبنائها . ويقال : ومن بناها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inspires the soul with wickedness and piety by abandoning or enabling it; another view takes them as the paths of good and evil.
rows.anchor: فجورها : حركتها في طلب الرزق ، وتقواها : سكونها بحكم القدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The successful person purifies the soul, or is purified by God.
rows.anchor: ويقال : من زكاه الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The failed soul may be one God has debased, hidden among the righteous despite not belonging to them, or one that a person debased through sin and made contemptible.
rows.anchor: وقيل : دسها في جملة الصالحين وليس منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamud disbelieved because of transgression; one account says Salih had died and God revived him, after which the people demanded a she-camel as a sign.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن صالحا قد مات ، فكفر قومه ، فأحياه الله ، فدعاهم إلى الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most wretched among them killed the she-camel; Salih warned them to leave God's camel and its drinking share alone.
rows.anchor: عاقرها . { فقال لهم رسول الله ناقة الله وسقياها } . أي : احذروا ناقة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God destroyed the people for their crime and leveled them; another explanation says all shared the same punishment because they approved the camel's slaughter.
rows.anchor: سوى بينهم ربهم في العذاب لأنهم كلهم رضوا بعقر الناقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not fear consequences for punishing the people.
rows.anchor: أن الله لا يخاف عاقبة ما فعل بهم من العقوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's lesson is that sustained worship and purification from sins, defects, reward-seeking, selfish interests, objection to one's allotment, and forbidden acts bring success.
rows.anchor: ويقال : قد أفلح من داوم على العبادة ، وخاب من قصر فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Failure comes from betraying and neglecting the soul, staining it with disobedience, and adding dark, false claims to its poverty.
rows.anchor: وقد خاب من خان نفسه ، وأهملها عن المراعاة ، ودنسها بالمخالفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night covers the horizon and the space between heaven and earth; for the bewildered, it also covers thought so they cannot find guidance.
rows.anchor: والليل لأصحاب التحير يستغرق جميع أقطار أفكارهم فلا يهتدون الرشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day becomes bright, clear, and manifest; for gnostics, inward lights disclose everything so they need no lamp.
rows.anchor: ونهار أهل العرفان بضياء قلوبهم وأسرارهم ، حتى لا يخفى عليهم شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath concerning male and female means the One who created them is God.
rows.anchor: أي : ( من ) خلق الذكر والأنثى ؛ وهو الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human striving differs: people pursue worldly life, desires, status, the afterlife, piety, remembrance, God's approval, or God Himself; others unite bodily obedience, sincerity, nearness, remembrance, good speech, and counsel.
rows.anchor: وآخر في طلب مولاه . ومنكم : من يجمع بين سعي النفس بالطاعة ، وسعي القلب بالإخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some people strive for their own ruin and the ruin of their worldly life.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من سعيه في هلاك نفسه وما فيه هلاك دنياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving can mean giving wealth, being fair to others without demanding fairness for oneself, or avoiding what displeases God.
rows.anchor: ويقال : { أعطى } الإنصاف من نفسه ، { واتقى } طلب الإنصاف لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good promise may mean Paradise, the final world, forgiveness of grave sinners, the Prophet's intercession, or God's compensation.
rows.anchor: بالجنة ، أو بالكرة الآخرة ، وبالمغفرة لأهل الكبائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes obedience easy, disobedience hateful, nearness desirable, faith beloved, and excellence attractive to the heart.
rows.anchor: أي نسهل عليه الطاعات ، ونكره إليه المخالفات ، ونشهي إليه القرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is continuing in God's obedience and returning to acts of worship already performed.
rows.anchor: الإقامة على طاعته والعود إلى ما عمله من عبادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The miser withholds what is obligatory, considers himself independent, and denies the promised good; God makes the path to hardship easy by bringing about sins and circumstances of disobedience.
rows.anchor: أما من منع الواجب ، واستغنى في اعتقاده ، وكذب بالحسنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss says that the giver turns away from both abodes and avoids assigning either a place in himself.
rows.anchor: أن يجعل لهما في نفسه مقدارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth cannot benefit its owner when he dies.
rows.anchor: وما يغنى عنه ماله إذا تردى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance is God's responsibility for those He guides, or the provision of evidences; both the present and next life belong to Him and are given as He wills.
rows.anchor: لأوليائنا ، الذين أرشدناهم . ويقال : { إن علينا للهدى } بنصيب الدلائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning is of a blazing fire; only the most wretched denier who turned away from faith enters it.
rows.anchor: أي : لا يعذب بها إلا الأشقى ، وهو : { الذي كذب وتولى } . يعني : كفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most God-fearing is kept from Hell and gives wealth to purify himself through obligatory alms or freedom from sin; the passage was revealed concerning Abu Bakr but applies generally.
rows.anchor: ونزلت الآية في أبي بكر رضي الله عنه ، والآية عامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He gives without repaying a favor or seeking to acquire an obligation from anyone; he gives only to seek God's countenance.
rows.anchor: ولا يفعل هذا ليتخذ عند أحد يدا ، ولا يطلب منه مكافأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will be pleased with him, and he will be pleased with what God gives him.
rows.anchor: يرضى الله عنه ، ويرضى هو بما يعطيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala affirms God's unique, wise, truthful, and faultless rule: His knowledge never lapses, His word is true, and all creation and dominion are His.
rows.anchor: فهو حكيم لا يلهو ، وعليم لا يسهو ، وحليم يثبت ويمحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍuḥā may mean a daytime hour, the whole day, the forenoon prayer, or the time when Moses spoke to God.
rows.anchor: ( والضحى ) : ساعة من النهار . أو النهار كل يسمى ضحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The still night may be the Night Journey, the general kind of night, the time of spiritual witnessing, or the night associated with the Prophet's report of a veil over his heart.
rows.anchor: ويقال : هو عام في جنس الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation relates the verse to God's descent to the lowest heaven at night, understood in a way compatible with divine attributes.
rows.anchor: حين ينزل الله فيه إلى السماء الدنيا - على التأويل الذي يصح في وصفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not stop revelation from Muhammad or hate him; this answered Meccans when Gabriel's visit was delayed for several days.
rows.anchor: ما قطع عنك الوحي وما أبغضك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports differ on Gabriel's absence: forty days, twelve days, or twenty-five days.
rows.anchor: وقيل : احتبس عنه جبريل أربعين يوما ، وقيل : اثني عشر يوما ، وقيل : خمسة وعشرين يوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says a Jewish question about Dhul-Qarnayn and the People of the Cave delayed the answer after Muhammad promised one without saying God willing.
rows.anchor: أن يهوديا سأله عن قصة ذي القرنين وأصحاب الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hereafter is better because its gifts exceed this world's; these include intercession, the Basin, and the robe of unity.
rows.anchor: ما يعطيك في الآخرة خير لك مما يعطيك في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When asked whether he would be satisfied with a gift apart from the Giver, Muhammad answered that he would not.
rows.anchor: قيل : أفترضى بالعطاء عن المعطي ؟ قال : لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sheltered the orphan Muhammad with his uncle Abu Talib; another reading says God nurtured him with care and brought him to an intimate station no one shared.
rows.anchor: قيل : إلى عمه أبي طالب . ويقال : بل آواه إلى كنف ظله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One outward account says Muhammad lost his way in Mecca's passes as a child until his uncle Abu Talib guided him.
rows.anchor: أي : ضللت في شعاب مكة ، فهدى إليك عمك أبا طالب في حال صباك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, being lost may mean bewilderment about God, then being guided by God to God; or lacking detailed religious rulings and being taught them.
rows.anchor: ويقال : ( ضالا ) فينا متحيرا . . فهديناك بنا إلينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings say Muhammad found wandering peoples and guided them, sought divine intimacy, or was lost in love and guided by the light of nearness.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ( ضالا ) في محبتنا ، فهديناك بنور القربة إلينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Further readings say God revealed His love for Muhammad, his noble rank, or made him known after he had been concealed among Meccans.
rows.anchor: عن محبتي لك فعرفتك أني أحبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God enriched Muhammad through Khadija's wealth, prophethood and scripture, sufficiency in God, contentment with deprivation, or by giving before he asked and freeing him from need to ask.
rows.anchor: ويقال : أغناك عن الإرداة والطلب بأن أرضاك بالفقد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not frighten orphans; treat them gently and draw them near.
rows.anchor: فلا تخفه ، وارفق به ، وقربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A petitioner should be helped or turned away gently, perhaps with a promise.
rows.anchor: أي : إما أن تعطيه . . أو ترده برفق ، أو وعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The petitioner may be someone asking about God or bewildered in God; do not rebuke them, since God will guide and uncover their questions, and speak gently.
rows.anchor: ويقال : السائل عنا ، والسائل المتحير فينا - لا تنهرهم ، فإنا نهديهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thank God by speaking openly of His kindness and the favors He granted you.
rows.anchor: فاشكر ، وصرح بإحسانه إليك ، وإنعامه عليك
